note.headline: Small caps and bonds rally together while curve flattens and gold jumps
note.standfirst: The Russell outperformed the Nasdaq by over a point as yields fell across the belly and long end and gold rose +2.06%. Positioning looks like a rotation into rate-sensitive cyclicals funded out of mega-cap tech, with credit and vol both confirming the risk-on read.
takeaways: Russell 2000 rose +1.38% while Nasdaq fell -0.05%, the clearest sign of rotation out of large-cap tech.
The curve flattened as 2-year yields rose +3bp while 10-year and 30-year yields fell -2bp and -4bp, a bid for duration at the long end even as the front end cheapened.
Gold rose +2.06% and silver rose +3.70% alongside a softer dollar, DXY down -0.53%, a combination that sits awkwardly with the risk-on equity tape.
VIX fell -2.43 points to 16.46 and high yield and investment grade credit both firmed, consistent with the broader risk barometer reading 0.62, constructive.
note.desk_view:
This session confirms a rotation trade, not a broad risk re-rating. The S&P rose +0.33% on the back of the Dow's +1.08% and the Russell's +1.38%, while the Nasdaq slipped -0.05% and Technology was the weakest S&P sector at -0.65%. Energy also lagged at -1.58% despite WTI up +1.08%, so this was not simply a cyclicals-up, defensives-down session. Breadth was healthy at 1.6 advancers to decliners, but the dispersion in sector returns, from Materials at +1.79% to Technology at -0.65%, says this was a stock and sector story more than an index story.

The level that decides whether this persists is the 10-year yield. It fell to 5.19%, extending a flattening move that has taken 2s10s down 5bp to 37bp, and that decline in long-end yields is doing real work for small caps, real estate (+1.21%) and financials (+1.38%), all of which carry duration sensitivity. If the 10-year stabilizes here or cheapens again, the rotation into rate-sensitive cyclicals loses its engine and money likely drifts back toward the mega-cap names that led the tape for most of this year. The gold move is the complication: a +2.06% rally in gold alongside a softer dollar and falling real yields (10-year TIPS down -4bp) reads more like a hedge against something than confirmation of the equity rotation, and that tension is worth watching into the next print.
watching: 10-year yield reaction if it tests back toward 5.19% support or breaks lower.
Whether Technology stabilizes or sees further rotation pressure after a -0.65% session.
Gold and silver follow-through, given the rally came with a weaker dollar and falling real yields.
High yield spreads, with JNK and HYG both printing new lows on the extremes list despite the day's gains.
note.equities:
The S&P closed up +0.33%, but the index return masks a clear split: the Dow rose +1.08% and the Russell 2000 rose +1.38%, while the Nasdaq fell -0.05%. Health care led the single-stock tape with LLY up +3.55% and UNH up +2.79%, and software and cloud names CRM and ORCL rose +4.57% and +3.00% respectively. NVDA and AMD were the laggards among large caps, down -1.84% and -1.50%, with semis absorbing the rotation out of Technology.

Sector dispersion was wide. Materials (+1.79%), Health care (+1.86%) and Consumer discretionary (+1.71%) led, while Energy (-1.58%) and Technology (-0.65%) were the only sectors in the red of size. Breadth confirmed the constructive tone, 16 advancers against 10 decliners, with dispersion at 1.67 suggesting this was a session of genuine stock-picking rather than an index-wide beta move.
note.rates:
The curve flattened again. 2s10s fell 5bp to 37bp and 5s30s fell 4bp to 52bp, with the front end cheapening (2-year up +3bp to 4.82%) while the long end firmed (30-year down -4bp to 5.52%, 10-year down -2bp to 5.19%). The 5-year held flat at 5.00%, leaving the belly as the pivot point of the move.

Breakevens softened alongside the bid for duration: the 5-year breakeven fell -3bp to 2.33% and 10-year TIPS yields fell -4bp to 2.84%. The MOVE index rose +3.46 points to 102.49 even as equity vol fell, a split that says rates markets are pricing more uncertainty into the path even as the direction today was clean.
note.credit: Credit firmed across the board. Investment grade (LQD) led with a +0.82% gain, high yield (HYG) rose +0.42% and EM sovereign debt (EMB) rose +0.67%. The firming in spread product lines up with the equity rally and the drop in VIX, but the extremes list flags JNK and HYG both printing new lows on a longer lookback, a reminder that today's gain is a bounce within a weaker trend rather than a change in it.
note.fx: The dollar index fell -0.53% to 102.006, with broad-based softness against G10: EUR/USD rose +0.17%, GBP/USD rose +0.11%, USD/CHF fell -0.75%. USD/JPY fell -0.23% to 157.964. The exception was the commodity bloc, where AUD/USD fell -0.87% despite the weaker dollar elsewhere. In EM, USD/BRL rose +1.46% and USD/TRY rose +0.25% to a fresh high, while USD/INR fell -0.25%, a mixed picture that does not read as a clean dollar story.
note.commodities: Gold rose +2.06% and silver rose +3.70%, with platinum up +2.13% and palladium up +4.50%, a broad precious metals bid against a softer dollar. WTI rose +1.08% while Brent fell -0.31%, a divergence worth noting in the oil complex. Copper fell -0.74%, breaking from the rest of the risk tape, and the ags were soft across the board: wheat -0.59%, corn -0.52%, soybeans -1.02%. Sugar made a fresh high, up +1.44%.
note.volatility: The vol surface eased across the curve. VIX fell -2.43 points to 16.46 and VIX9D fell -4.25 points to 13.97, steepening the front end of the term structure and signaling less near-term hedging demand. VVIX fell -1.99 to 92.57, but SKEW rose +2.00 to 160.45, so the cost of tail protection crept higher even as at-the-money vol came in. That combination says the market bought calm day-to-day while still paying up for downside insurance.
note.digital: Bitcoin rose +0.94%, a modest gain that lagged the equity rally and continues a weak year, down -7.21% YTD. Ether, Solana and XRP all posted small gains of similar magnitude, +1.68%, +1.76% and +0.72% respectively. The muted beta to the equity and credit rally suggests digital assets are trading on their own narrower flows today rather than tracking the broader risk tape.
note.international: European markets were mixed into the New York open: the EURO STOXX 50 fell -0.36% and the DAX rose +0.33%, with the FTSE 100 up +1.08% and the FTSE MIB down -0.72%. Asia closed mostly softer, Nikkei down -0.05%, Hang Seng down -0.13%, KOSPI down -0.44%, with the TAIEX the outlier at +0.59%. Neither region showed the rotation pattern that defined the US session, leaving New York to generate its own small-cap, long-duration bid independent of the overnight tape.
note.correlation:
The standout cross-asset signal today is the simultaneous rally in equities, credit and gold against a falling dollar and lower long-end yields. Normally a risk-on equity session with tightening credit spreads sits alongside a firmer dollar and higher real yields, not a drop in both. Today's setup, S&P up, HYG up, gold up, DXY down, 10-year yield down, looks more like a broad decline in the dollar's opportunity cost than a single equity risk impulse.

A break in this correlation would show up first in gold and the dollar moving back in their usual inverse lockstep without equities confirming, or in the MOVE index, up +3.46 today, continuing to rise while VIX continues to fall. That divergence between rates vol and equity vol is already present and bears watching: if rates volatility keeps climbing while equity vol keeps compressing, the two markets are pricing different distributions of the same macro outcome, and one of them is wrong.
